answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed identity: before an agent can transact, it must lock a refundable deposit in a common vault. A single honest agent pays once, but an attacker trying to flood the network with fake identities must fund every copy, so the cost scales with the size of the fraud. If a fake misbehaves, its deposit is slashed, turning a cheap ocean of sock puppets into an expensive, self-defeating operation, unlike saffron, which is valuable precisely because it cannot be mass-produced for free.
